title: Aging‐Induced Ductile‐Brittle‐Ductile Transition in High‐Entropy Alloys and its Implications

recollection.starting_material: High-entropy alloys (likely a CoCrFeMnNi or similar system)
recollection.intervention: Aging treatment at elevated temperatures for varying durations
recollection.structure: A transition from a ductile state to a brittle state and back to a ductile state as a function of aging time
recollection.mechanism: Precipitation of secondary phases causing initial embrittlement, followed by phase dissolution or microstructural coarsening restoring ductility
recollection.results: A non-monotonic change in fracture toughness and yield strength, with a minimum ductility at an intermediate aging time

score.note: The recollection only generically identifies aging and repeats the title-level ductile–brittle–ductile transition, incorrectly framing it mainly as aging-time dependent. It does not identify AlCoCrFeNi2.1, the 600°C/750°C treatments, enhanced L12 ordering, jagged B2/FCC boundaries, or ductile boundary transition zones. The proposed precipitation/dissolution mechanism is incorrect, and no quantitative temperatures or property values are recalled.
